title: Config-variant latency/quality watchlist and eval harness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build a repeatable, canary-grade evaluation and watchlist for configuration variants that trade latency vs. model output quality. This ticket delivers (1) an experiment harness to run controlled comparisons of batching and KV-cache config variants against traffic-replay and synthetic workloads, (2) an analysis pipeline that computes token- and request-level quality deltas plus latency distributions and tail behavior, and (3) automated alerting/rollback rules that surface unacceptable regressions before platform-wide rollout.

Scope and motivation:
- Recent config changes (max_batch_wait_ms, microbatch thresholds, prefix-KV caching heuristics) have shown non-linear effects on tail latency and output fidelity for multi-turn chat workloads. We need a defensible, automated method to quantify these tradeoffs tied to PRs and runtime releases.

Core deliverables:
1) Harness: a lightweight runner that can execute variants side-by-side against: (a) recorded production traffic (traffic-replay), (b) curated eval prompt suites (QA, instruction-following, code), and (c) synthetic long-context sequences designed to stress KV cache warmup. Outputs: per-request traces (latency histograms, token counts), model outputs, token-level probabilities when available.
2) Metric suite: standardized metric set including: P50/P95/P99 latency (total and server-side), input-to-first-byte, tokens/sec, hallucination-rate (heuristic + classifier), response-consistency (embedding cosine vs baseline), instruction-following score (task-specific rubric), and ROUGE/BLEU-like ngram overlap for deterministic tasks. Define delta thresholds and expected noise bands.
3) Variant matrix & orchestration: prepare experiments covering combinations of: microbatch_size (1,4,8), max_batch_wait_ms (0,5,20,50), enable_prefix_cache (on/off), cache_eviction_window (short/medium/long), and kv_cache_warm_fraction (10/50/90%). Each variant runs N=1000 replayed requests + curated evals. Use randomized seed and stable tokenizer to avoid artefacts.
4) Analysis pipeline: end-to-end job that ingests traces + outputs, computes paired statistical tests (bootstrap CIs, A/B delta), and outputs a summary report with: quality vs latency frontier, statistically significant regressions flagged, and suggested action (approve, canary, rollback).
5) Watchlist and alerts: integrate with Console dashboards and create a watchlist where ongoing rollouts post metrics. Define automatic fail criteria (e.g., quality delta > 2% absolute for critical prompt set OR P99 latency increase > 30% while throughput falls) to gate deployments.

Experiment details (unique approach):
- Use a layered evaluation: overall aggregate + per-prompt cohort. Cohorts include short instruction prompts, long-context summarization, multi-turn chat with state, and code-generation. This surfaces config brittleness tied to workload shape.
- Use embedding-similarity + a small hallucination classifier to catch semantic regressions that ngram overlap misses.
- Compute cost proxy (tokens * per-token cost estimate) to estimate per-request unit economics for each variant and include that on the frontier.
- Track warmup dynamics: run long replay streams and measure quality/latency as a function of time since restart to expose cache warmup/decay effects.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1 (this ticket): Assemble harness skeleton, wire in traffic-replay connector, and implement logging/tracing format.
- Week 2: Implement metric computations and paired-analysis; run smoke tests for 3 variants; land PRs for data collection.
- Week 3: Run full matrix on staging dataset (N=1000 per variant), produce report, and finalize alert threshold proposals.
- Week 4: Integrate watchlist into Console dashboards and create rollout guard policy for runtime-1.20.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run the full variant matrix automatically and produce a JSON report with all metrics.
- Report includes confidence intervals and explicit recommendations (approve/canary/rollback).
- Alerts wired to Console and an initial run against staging produced a non-trivial report that caught at least one regression in our staged config changes.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EVALS/Config-Variant-Eval-Harness (draft)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 (harness + metrics)
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ev-harness-24890 (staging)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: traffic-replay fidelity differs from real traffic (missing live cache effects). Mitigation: include long live-like streams and validate warmup curves vs canary observability.
- Risk: quality metrics noisy for low-frequency prompts. Mitigation: use cohort-level aggregation and bootstrap to estimate uncertainty; require larger N for low-frequency cohorts.

Next steps after acceptance:
- Automate per-PR gating: run the harness for config-change PRs and post results to PRs and the Console.
- Expand prompt suites using customer-sourced examples under NDA to improve coverage.

Owners: Liam Chen (lead), Aisha Kapoor (eval design), Sofia Martínez (observability integration).
